interpretations_review.outcome: Both complete constructions have distinct source-supported arguments; Mark reception repair required
interpretations_review.A: Rightful earthly dues under the universal Creator; Jerome distinguishes Cyrus from Christ, Chrysostom bounds civil obedience by godliness, Augustine universal worship and Aquinas image-of-God extension contribute different reasoning. Each element and all four senses have specified roles; complete formulary synthesis is labeled editorial.
interpretations_review.B: Divine gift precedes and enables willing fruitful service; Aquinas on Phil2 supplies inward willing and acting without fatalism or prior merit, Chrysostom links faith/love/hope to costly endurance, and Psalm32 reception explains received food and hope. Its causal movement differs from A while preserving the Gospel civil sense.
interpretations_review.limits: No requirement imposed for the superseded gallery/proposal quotas, author commentaries on every element, or invented disagreement.

consequential_difficulty_tests.locus: Jerome, In Isaiam XII on45:1-7, DCO Pars3 physical126-129; Aquinas In Isaiam45 [85005]
consequential_difficulty_tests.question: Does calling the unknowing Cyrus anointed identify him directly with Christ or justify his religion?
consequential_difficulty_tests.result: No. Jerome rejects the direct identification because of the ignorance clause yet allows type/image; Aquinas distinguishes office and divine benefit from the king remaining idolatrous. The research preserves that difficulty and result.

consequential_difficulty_tests.locus: Chrysostom, In Matthaeum LXX1-2; Aquinas Super Matthaeum22 lectio2 [87389]
consequential_difficulty_tests.question: Does render Caesar erase the boundary of obedience or does image spirituality replace the literal tribute problem?
consequential_difficulty_tests.result: No. Chrysostom expressly restricts civil dues to what does not harm godliness. Aquinas explicitly marks the soul-image application mystical and retains civic peace. Research A retains the literal trap and bounded spiritual extension.

consequential_difficulty_tests.locus: Aquinas Super Philippenses2 lectio3 [87838] and lectio4 [87839]; Chrysostom PhilippiansVIII, especially the word-of-life paragraph and NPNF note637
consequential_difficulty_tests.question: Does grace replace free agency, and do author and editor teach the same word-of-life interpretation?
consequential_difficulty_tests.result: No. Aquinas rejects both unaided human willing and fatalism; Chrysostom describes a principle/seed of life while the editorial note objects. Research B and the comparison table retain the distinction.

consequential_difficulty_tests.locus: Augustine Enarrationes PsXCV/EnglishXCVI §§2,6,9,11,14-15; OLM145A Psalm strophe
consequential_difficulty_tests.question: May from the wood or the fixed-world clause be treated as appointed wording?
consequential_difficulty_tests.result: No. They support a Christian reception reading only; the research correctly excludes the added lemma and omitted10b from the appointment.

consequential_difficulty_tests.locus: Augustine Enarrationes PsXXXII/EnglishXXXIII §§16-22; Aquinas Super Psalmo32 nn15-17 [87102-87104]
consequential_difficulty_tests.question: Does food in famine promise bodily immunity?
consequential_difficulty_tests.result: The sources develop dependence, Word, sacrament and final hope; Aquinas distinguishes bodily, spiritual and final rescue. Research does not turn the antiphon into immunity.

consequential_difficulty_tests.locus: Gregory Nazianzen OrationXLV §§21-24, especially22; Aquinas STIII q48 a4 and beginninga5
consequential_difficulty_tests.question: Can their ransom accounts be flattened into agreement about a payment demanded by the Father?
consequential_difficulty_tests.result: No. Gregory denies such demand and emphasizes acceptance/sanctification; Aquinas positively describes the satisfaction-price paid to God, not the devil. The research retains this real difference without manufacturing doctrinal contradiction.

finding_evidence.locus: Bede, In Marci evangelium expositio III, on Mark10:42-45, transmitted PL92 columns236A-B, especially236B
finding_evidence.inspection: Read the full direct lemma and its preceding contrast of worldly power with humility in the electronic Latin transcript; transcript credits Migne and Corpus Corporum. No historical facsimile inspection claimed.
finding_evidence.material_result: Bede explains Son of Man through the servant-form, connects the blood shed for the world with many understood as those willing to believe, and thus directly engages the appointed clause and the response-to-gift problem. Current research contains no Bede search/disposition and no developed account of this phrase. A broad web search independently found the DCO text as corroborating discovery evidence; its PDF open failed, so it is not the inspected witness.
